## Analysis

The diff removes `case 'year':` from the years branch of the parse switch and replaces it with `case "":`.

Two things to check:

1. **Is `case "":` reachable?** The regex captures the unit as either `undefined` (when the optional group doesn't participate, e.g. `ms('5')`) or a non-empty string — no alternative in the group can match empty. And `(match[2] || 'ms')` coerces both `undefined` and `''` to `'ms'`. So `case "":` is dead code; it changes nothing.

2. **Is `case 'year':` needed?** Yes. The regex `...|years?|yrs?|y` still captures `match[2] === 'year'` for inputs like `'1 year'` or `'1year'`. In the original 2.1.3 code, `type === 'year'` hits `case 'year'` and returns `n * y` (e.g. `ms('1 year') === 31557600000`). After the patch, `'year'` falls through to `default: return undefined`, so `ms('1 year')` returns `undefined`.

The library's own suite doesn't exercise the bare singular `'year'` spelling (it tests `'1y'`, `'1yr'`, etc.), which is why it stays green — but this is an observable regression for any caller passing `"1 year"`, a very natural input.

```json
{
  "defect": true,
  "testFile": {
    "path": "proof-test.js",
    "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('fails on the patched build', function () {\n    // 'year' (singular) must still parse as one year\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1 year'), 31557600000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1year'), 31557600000);\n  });\n});\n"
  },
  "note": "Removing case 'year' makes ms('1 year') (and '1year') fall through to the switch's default and return undefined instead of 31557600000, since the unchanged regex still captures the unit as 'year'. The added case \"\" is unreachable, so the only effect is this regression."
}
```
